crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Ledger Anomaly Detection
children.blurb: Ledger anomaly detection in continuous audit and assurance uses automated checks to find unusual entries, patterns, or balances in general ledgers and subledgers that may indicate error, fraud, or control failure.

children.name: Substantive Testing at Full Coverage
children.blurb: Substantive testing at full coverage means applying audit procedures to every transaction or record in a population rather than a sample.

children.name: Inventory Observation and Valuation
children.blurb: This page covers the use of artificial intelligence in the continuous audit and assurance of inventory observation and valuation.

children.name: Going Concern Analysis
children.blurb: Going concern analysis in continuous audit and assurance assesses whether a company can meet its obligations for at least twelve months from the reporting date.

children.name: Internal Control Testing
children.blurb: Internal control testing is the process of evaluating whether controls over financial reporting, operations, and compliance are designed appropriately and operating effectively.

sections.body: Continuous audit and assurance uses artificial intelligence to check financial records and controls on an ongoing basis rather than once a year. In practice, machine learning models scan general ledgers for unusual entries, compare transactions against expected patterns, and flag items for human review. For substantive testing, AI can examine every transaction in a population instead of a sample, looking for duplicate payments, missing approvals, or mismatched amounts. Inventory observation now includes image recognition and sensor data to count stock or estimate valuation, while going concern analysis uses models that read financial statements and news to assess whether a company can stay solvent. Internal control testing uses process mining and natural language processing to check whether controls are actually followed.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is real but uneven. Ledger anomaly detection is the most mature, with many accounting firms and software vendors offering tools that reliably flag outliers, though false positives remain common and require skilled judgment. Substantive testing at full coverage is technically possible for structured data, but messy source systems, inconsistent formats, and the need to explain findings still limit how much can be fully automated. Inventory observation works well in warehouses with fixed cameras or RFID tags, but physical counts in less controlled environments still need human verification. Going concern analysis is the least settled, because predicting insolvency involves forward-looking judgment, incomplete information, and legal risk, and no model can replace an auditor's opinion. Internal control testing can identify when a control was bypassed in a system log, but it cannot easily assess the intent behind a manual override or the quality of a review.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader wanting to understand how AI spots suspicious entries should start with Ledger Anomaly Detection, which explains the core techniques and their limits. Substantive Testing at Full Coverage builds on that by showing what happens when auditors stop sampling and test every record, including the practical obstacles. Inventory Observation and Valuation moves from ledgers to physical assets, covering how sensors and images feed into counts and pricing. Going Concern Analysis shifts to a forward-looking question, using the same data sources but with much higher uncertainty. Internal Control Testing closes the loop by examining whether the processes that produce the ledger are themselves reliable, which is the foundation for trusting any of the other pages.
